review: Reviewed Moss's round-8 request and the accepted world-13 develop review (learning 3). Implemented cultivate-plant@1 in scope long-ex14 as a general, actor-independent operation named by function, with modes plant, resume, cancel, inspect, tend and remove. Following the specification's own fallback, the existing root resource has no propagating structure, growth, biomass or yield model, so no supported facts establish viable material: the executable precursor is a physical planting trial with recorded survival or decay, and replenishment remains unverified. Plant uses exactly one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1 enforced), an unoccupied ordinary-soil 0.2-radius plot in reach, and two paid work rounds of 1 energy each with exact escrow, interruption, resume, cancel and death handling; the unit is transferred into the plot, never duplicated, and keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Inspect is the unchanged baseline probe observation (one round, 0.2 energy, visible state only, existing evidence-deduplicated feedback), not a new diagnostic. Tend is unavailable and spends nothing: plots are made on bare soil, no competing cover is represented on them in this scope, and irrigation needs an implemented water input. Remove (one round, 1 energy, planter only) returns only physically remaining material and leaves an emptied plot. No growth, harvest, food, comfort or satisfaction rule is added and no reward for planting, inspecting or removing. Assumptions recorded: one unit per trial; reach 0.65 plus body radius; no hidden viability is shown. Reuse: the ex13 root-planting-trial@1 placement, escrow and ageing code is parameterized by plot revision and work-state key with ex13 defaults unchanged, plus collective-work and the baseline probe; this is recorded implementation reuse, not reinvention, and no ex13 ability, plot or mastery is inherited. Visuals reuse the existing plant component with prepared, planted-unverified and decayed states. Tests cover scope, study, paid planting, conservation, inspection, refused tending, no food growth and planter-only removal.
